assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling between a single microwave photon and a superconducting artificial atom routine and controllable on a chip. It created the architecture for dispersive readout, qubit-qubit coupling via resonators and microwave quantum optics on chip, and underpins essentially all superconducting quantum processors. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are very high, and it is a clean case of a basic quantum phenomenon becoming an enabling platform.
assessment.attribution: Blais (with Huang, Girvin, Schoelkopf) supplied the 2004 theory proposal, and Wallraff with Schoelkopf and colleagues delivered the 2004 Nature strong-coupling experiment. Three laureates is a natural configuration. Girvin, Huang and others are not in the supplied credited names, so the allocation leaves out some who contributed decisively; I cannot resolve this within the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently across many laboratories and platforms for two decades, with a stable interpretation. Timing is mature, though the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits is a close neighbour and the committee may judge that field recently recognised.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to recognise superconducting circuits again so soon after the 2025 prize.
Omitted contributors such as Girvin and Huang to the theory proposal; I rely on memory for the exact credit history.
As a researcher in this field with close ties to these groups, I should flag possible conflict of interest for my own assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, trapped many atoms free of Doppler and recoil shifts and reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It opened a new regime of precision for tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The discovery is clear, original and has had measurable consequences.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the strontium clock; Ye's group drove it to record accuracy and many-body clock physics. Other contributors, notably Lemonde and Takamoto, may be discussed, but two laureates are a coherent and fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups worldwide with consistent performance, and the interpretation is robust. Not premature, though earlier clock-related prizes (Hall and Hansch 2005, Wineland 2012) mean the committee must be convinced this is a distinct enough step.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for frequency combs and ion clocks.
Whether the redefinition of the second, still pending, would make recognition better timed later.
I am recalling some priority details from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators opened a major class of topological phases of matter protected by time-reversal symmetry, with helical edge states observed in HgTe wells. It generated a large and still active field and a new classification of band structures. Impact and originality are high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theory of the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall state; Molenkamp's group made the 2007 experimental observation following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied credit omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and others like Zhang and Moore, Balents and Roy, Fu and Kane share credit for 3D topological insulators, so allocation is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation has been extensive in HgTe and later in 3D materials via ARPES, but quantised edge conductance was cleanly seen in few systems. The field is mature, and Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz 2016 already recognised topology in matter.
uncertainties: Contested credit among Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents and others.
Possible view that this is partly covered by the 2016 prize.
Condensed matter beyond my core expertise, so I defer to colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Mott insulator transition and then quantum gas microscopes, giving controllable Hubbard-model quantum simulators. It opened a new regime of tunable many-body physics with single-site resolution and is clear and important.
assessment.attribution: Bloch and Greiner led the key experiments (Mott transition 2002, quantum gas microscopy), while Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) provided the theory proposal. I propose the two experimentalists here, with Zoller better placed in the trapped-ion entry; the supplied credit does not include Jaksch.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many labs and widely used as a platform; interpretation stable. Timing seems ripe, although the simulation of problems not accessible classically is still a developing claim.
uncertainties: Whether quantum simulation advantage claims are mature enough.
Split of credit between experiment and theory, and the omission of Jaksch from the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal showed how to do quantum logic with trapped ions, and experiments (Blatt, plus Wineland's already-recognised NIST work) demonstrated entangling gates and small algorithms. It established a key platform for quantum information and has far-reaching influence, including on quantum simulation.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive 1995 theoretical proposal, and Blatt's group led several landmark experiments on gate implementation and entanglement of ions. Wineland's 2012 prize partly overlaps; Monroe, Wineland and others are not in the supplied names, so this configuration is arguable but supportable.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed, with commercial ion-trap processors. The question is whether the 2012 prize for controlling single quantum systems makes this redundant.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize to Wineland and Haroche.
Experimental credit relative to Monroe and Wineland groups is not resolved by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light below the shot-noise limit was proposed by Caves for interferometers, demonstrated by Kimble's group and others, and now improves gravitational-wave detectors. It is a clear case of quantum optics turned into a working instrument improvement.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the theory, Kimble the first squeezed-light experiments, and Schnabel the long-term development for GEO600 and LIGO-class detectors. Walls, Slusher, Yuen and others are not credited, so allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and in routine use in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600. The gravitational-wave detection itself was recognised in 2017; the squeezing step is a later, narrower contribution.
uncertainties: Attribution among Caves, Yuen, Walls, Slusher, Kimble and Schnabel is not clear from the supplied names.
The case relies on being a distinct step from the 2017 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the entanglement-based Ekert protocol founded quantum cryptography, linking foundations of quantum mechanics to a practical information-security idea. Conceptual originality is high and the field is now commercial and satellite-demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84 and Ekert the entanglement-based E91 protocol, a natural three-person configuration; Wiesner's earlier conjugate coding and credit for teleportation are a possible dispute.
assessment.maturity: The core principles are proven, with decades of experiments, but practical security and the scope of the discovery are still debated. The 2022 prize partially covered entanglement and Bell tests.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on entanglement.
Whether it is a physics discovery or an information-theory invention.
Wiesner's priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed flat bands and correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable system, opening twistronics. Originality is very high and the field is extremely active.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018. Cao and others as first authors, and Kim, Dean and others for related work, are not credited. The configuration is reasonable but not settled.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in several groups, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet stable. Probably early for a prize.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and phase diagram unresolved.
Possible prematurity.
Credit between theory and experiment and the roles of Cao and other collaborators.
